title: hamza-grades

errors.description: letterGrade uses `points > 90` instead of `points >= 90`, so a score of exactly 90 returns 'B' rather than 'A', contradicting the comment 'and above'.
classAverage does not guard against an empty scores array; when scores.length is 0 the function divides by zero and returns NaN.
errors.suggestion: Add an early return of 0 (or throw) when scores.length === 0, before the division.

errors.description: topStudents calls scores.sort() directly, which mutates the caller's original array in-place as an unintended side-effect.
errors.suggestion: Sort a shallow copy instead: `const ranked = [...scores].sort((a, b) => b.points - a.points)`.

errors.description: passRate filters with `s.points > 60` (strict greater-than), so a student with exactly 60 points is excluded despite the stated rule 'passed (60 or more)'.
medianPoints calls .sort() without a numeric comparator, causing lexicographic (string) ordering of numbers (e.g. [9, 80] sorts as [80, 9]), producing wrong medians.
errors.suggestion: Pass a numeric comparator: `.sort((a, b) => a - b)`.

errors.description: medianPoints always picks the single upper-middle index for even-length arrays instead of averaging the two middle values, so the median is incorrect for even-sized inputs.
errors.suggestion: For even-length arrays, return the average of sorted[mid - 1] and sorted[mid] where mid = sorted.length / 2.

analysis.summary: The file contains six issues across four functions. Two boundary-condition bugs (letterGrade off-by-one on 90, passRate off-by-one on 60) will produce wrong grades and pass-rate percentages. classAverage will crash with NaN on an empty input. topStudents silently mutates the caller's array. medianPoints is broken for all inputs because it sorts numbers as strings, and additionally computes an incorrect median for even-length arrays.

fixes.change: Changed `points > 90` to `points >= 90` in letterGrade so a score of exactly 90 correctly returns 'A'.
Added an early `if (scores.length === 0) return 0` guard in classAverage to prevent division by zero returning NaN on an empty array.
Changed `scores.sort(...)` to `[...scores].sort(...)` in topStudents to sort a shallow copy and avoid mutating the caller's original array.
Changed `s.points > 60` to `s.points >= 60` in passRate so students with exactly 60 points are correctly counted as passing.
Added a numeric comparator `(a, b) => a - b` to the `.sort()` call in medianPoints to prevent lexicographic ordering of numbers.
Updated medianPoints to average the two middle elements for even-length arrays instead of always returning the upper-middle index.

report.summary: Six bugs were found across four functions in the grades module, all rated High or Medium risk. Two off-by-one boundary errors (letterGrade at 90, passRate at 60) produced wrong letter grades and pass-rate percentages; classAverage returned NaN on empty input due to division by zero; topStudents silently mutated the caller's array; and medianPoints was broken for all inputs because it sorted numbers lexicographically, and additionally computed the wrong median for even-length arrays. All six issues were fixed, and 27 tests now guard against each regression.
recommendations: Add input-validation or TypeScript overloads to enforce non-empty arrays where NaN is not a valid return.
Enable a lint rule (e.g. eslint-plugin-unicorn's no-array-sort-mutation) to catch in-place sort side-effects.
Add boundary-value test cases (e.g. exactly-threshold scores) to the project's standard test suite.
Run the 27 generated tests in CI to prevent regressions on all fixed issues.
